How to play

  1. Pinch, scroll or double-tap on a glowing edge to dive in.
  2. Keep going. The detail never runs out.
  3. Turn on Julia mode and tap a spot to see its Julia set.

What's happening?

  • Every pixel is a number. The computer takes it, squares it and adds the start number back, again and again.
  • If the answer stays small forever, the pixel is in the set: it's painted dark.
  • If the answer shoots off to infinity, the colour shows how fast it escaped.
  • That one tiny rule makes a shape whose edge has endless detail. Zoom in anywhere on the edge and you'll find new spirals, and even tiny copies of the whole set.
  • A Julia set uses the same rule, but keeps one number fixed. Each spot on the Mandelbrot set has its own Julia set. Spots inside give solid shapes; spots outside give dust.
  • The computer only keeps about 16 digits. At about 1013× zoom it runs out, and the picture goes blocky.

Try this: find a tiny copy of the whole Mandelbrot set hiding somewhere along the edge. Hint: follow the long spike on the left. Bookmark it when you do!
